children: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, rose to its highest since late 2023 on Wednesday, buoyed by strong rates across all segments.
, which tracks rates for capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, added 174 points, or 5.5%, to reach 3,331, its highest since December 2023.
The capesize index (.BACI) was up 421 points, or 8.1%, at 5,642, its highest level since December 2023.
Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, rose $3,819 to $47,666.
However, iron ore futures fell as rising coking coal costs continued to squeeze steel mill margins and growing port inventories underscored ample supply.
The panamax index (.BPNI) gained 69 points, or 2.9%, to reach 2,429, hitting a more than three-month high.
Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, increased $628 to $21,865.
Among smaller vessels, the supramax index (.BSIS) was up 7 points, or 0.4%, at 1,657.
